summary: Gary Snyder works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and other fields. He studied at Reed College, Indiana University, UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, and with Isshu Miura and Sesso Oda. He held posts at UC Davis (1986) and UC Irvine (2002).

Gary Urton works in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. He taught at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (~2002–2020).
Gary Wee Kian Goh works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Hui-Chieh Loy, foster supervisor Jay L. Garfield, Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the Diocesan Seminary of Mondovì, the University of Turin under Amedeo Peyron, and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held posts at Turin's Military Academy, University, and Royal and National University Libraries.

Gaston Paris was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez (~1856–1858) and at the École des chartes (~1858–1862). He held appointments at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique from approximately 1898 to 1900.

Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and he taught Shenphen Nangwa and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima.

Gauri Viswanathan works in Indology and other fields. She studied at the University of Delhi (~1968–1972) and Columbia University (PhD, 1985). She taught English at Delhi and became Class of 1933 Professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia (~1989).

Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Birmingham under John Hick (~1980–1983) and Cambridge (~1983–1985). He held posts at the West London Institute (~1985–1989) and the University of Bristol (from 1993, emeritus professor of Catholic theology).

Gavin Flood specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Lancaster University (~1984–1988) under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. His posts include Lampeter (~1991–1998), Stirling (~2005–2008), Oxford and the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (2005–2015), and Yale-NUS College (2016).
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indologist. She is a doctoral student at the University of Tübingen under supervisor Claire Maes and holds a faculty post there (attested 2026).

Gelek works in Tibetology and other fields. He has served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998), a visiting lecturer at the University of California, and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rimpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell, training under Ling, Trijang, Denma Lochö, and Zong Rinpoches. He was director of Tibet House, New Delhi (1965).

Gembo Dorji works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Tango Buddhist Institute, East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, and with traditional teachers Tenzin Dhendrup, Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Jigme Choedra, Dralop Kuenlay Gyeltshen, Sonam Jamtsho, Sangay Dorji, and Sendrak Rinpoche.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959, doctorate 1991). He served as a researcher at the Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies and Toyo Bunko (~1962–1974), and as professor at Kokugakuin University (2006).

Genchi Kato worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue. His appointments included the Imperial Japanese Army (1906–1933), Army War College (1907), University of Tokyo (1920–1933), Kokugakuin University (1933), and Taisho University (1933).
Gendun Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who served as abbot and retreat master at Dhagpo Kagyu Ling from approximately 1977 to 1997.

Gendün Chöphel was a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history. He studied at Drisha, Labrang, Kumbum (under Gendun Tendzin Gyatso), and Drepung Monasteries, as well as under Sherab Gyatso. He held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society (1941).
Geng Shimin was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China from ~1949 to 1953 and held a post there from ~1953 to 2000.

Genjun Sasaki was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and with various teachers, including Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat and Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He held posts at Hamburg (1956), Otani University (attested 1974–1995), and Osaka University (attested 1995).
